newsitem.title: CHILE: Bullish momentum builds in Latin American stocks.
newsitem.headline: Bullish momentum builds in Latin American stocks.

text.p: Latin American stocks are likely to push higher this week on strong foreign buying and as speculation eases that the Federal Reserve will jack up interest rates, said analysts.
On the region's five main bourses, prices were generally expected to climb this week on a mixture of foreign and domestic factors, with only Buenos Aires seen holding flat, they said.

"Prices look strong and much less volatile than a couple of weeks ago. The outlook is basically positive,"said Enrique Danoni, analyst at Santiago brokers Sud Americano, talking about the Chilean market, although his sentiment summed up feeling in much of Latin America.

But problems persist in the Chilean electrical sector, the biggest single industry on the Santiago bourse. Power utilities are being forced to buy electricity at markups to compensate for the effects of drought on reservoirs, dragging down profits, said Danoni.

He saw better prospects in the paper pulp sector, especially at Copec, while traders also pointed to strong foreign buying. The selective index ended Friday at 120.60 points, up one percent for the week and a high for the year.
In Mexico, stocks were seen extending their gains as fears receded of a large hike in U.S. interest rates at a key Federal Reserve meeting on May 20, analysts said.
They forecast a rise of no more than 25 basis points in the benchmark rate -- a rise already factored into prices.

"It's too early for profit-takers to step in. The movement is only just beginning," said Carlos Samano, head of research at Mexico's Bancomer brokerage. He saw a drop in domestic rates giving further impetus to the market.

"Domestic rates should come down because of enhanced market liquidity, government spending is behind schedule and many firms pay out profit-sharing schemes in May," he said. Mexico's blue-chip IPC closed Friday at 3,873.38 points, up 2.88 percent for the week.

Brazilian shares were also expected to firm this week, on optimism that Congress will pass a bill setting rules for privatization of the telecoms industry in the coming months. Higher bidding for the Band B cellular phone business has also boosted prices, brokers said. "The market continues to be upbeat on telecoms," said a senior trader. Sao Paulo shares ended 4.1 percent higher last week at 10,491 points.

Strong foreign demand was expected to boost blue chips in Venezuela, where Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said the International Monetary Fund shared official forecasts of up to four percent growth this year and five percent in 1998.
"Blue chips look good...foreign funds are building up positions because they see good long-term prospects for the economy," said Banplus broker Alberto Briceno.
The Caracas bourse's 19-share index ended Friday at 6,585.58 points, up 3.5 percent for the week, as foreign investors snapped up stocks with American Depositary Receipts.

The outlook was more sober in Buenos Aires, where stocks were expected to stay locked in a tight range and focus on the release of U.S. inflation indicators before the Fed's meeting May 20, dealers said.

"There will be a wait-and-see attitude in the final countdown to the Fed talks," said Gabriel Armando at Argentine brokers Galicia Valores. "If the Fed hikes rates we may drift sideways for a while longer; but if it doesn't, stocks should embark on a sold recovery."

On the local front, investors were awaiting details of the planned $3 billion sale of the National Mortgage Bank and news from an IMF team currently in Buenos Aires studying a new loan deal. The Merval slipped 1.2 percent last week to 723.78 points but still stands fractionally higher so far in May.
